text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London remained under pressure following sharp declines in New York. Fund players liquidated positions as sell stops were triggered but bargain hunters were quick to move in and snap up bargains at the lows. July closed $125 lower at $1,695 per tonne. September lost $115 to close at $1,735 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York closed sharply lower across the board with front month July loosing 10.30 cents/lb to close at 207.65 cents/lb, while September gave up 6.65 cents/lb to close at 190.10 cents/lb. Forecasts of mild temperatures in Brazil were again behind the fall in coffee prices. Moreover, buyers were unwilling to step up demand and secure additional supplies even though availability could tighten again later in the year.
There was little reaction to news that Colombian production in May 1997 was more than 12 per cent higher than during the same month the previous year.

COLOMBIA - The Colombian Coffee Federation recently estimated 1996/97 (October/September) coffee production to reach about 10 million bags, down from 12.9 million bags produced the previous year. That estimate was based on a production figure for May of 1 million bags but actual output was not more than 836,000 bags, up from 745,000 bags the same month last year.

This brought total production from October 1996 through May 1997 up to 7.29 million bags, down from 9.9 million bags the same period in 1995/96. This suggests that the total for 1996/97 will be between 9.6 and 9.7 million bags. Allowing for domestic consumption of about 1.5 million bags only 8.1 to 8.2 million bags would be available for export compared to export commitments of some 11 million bags. This means that the federation will have to draw extensively on stocks to meet export schedules.

However, the federation has admitted that much of the stocks are not fresh crop. Private exporters believe that much of the officially cited 4 million bags stocks are beans from harvests between 1995 and 1991. It is estimated that 1997/98 production might improve to about 12.0-12.5 million bags but trade sources pointed out that the crop is running very late and hence supplies will need to be stretched that much further, particularly in the United States.

BRAZIL - Brazil exported 1.33 million 60-kg bags of coffee ground and in beans, in May, up from an adjusted April figure of 1.22 million bags and exports of 695,815 bags in May last year. Previously Febec had estimated April exports at 1.21 million bags. Brazilian exports so far this year have reached 6.46 million bags, more than twice the 3.01 million bags shipped in the first five months of 1996.

Under the ACPC retention scheme Brazil is not allowed to ship more than 6 million bags in the first half of 1997 and the country has officially notified the ACPC that it has overshot its target of coffee exports. The larger-than- expected shipments are because all private stocks have been sold, the soluble industry has exported less and producers have also taken advantage of high international prices, official sources said.

However, the Brazilians claimed, that also other countries have exceeded their export limits. Given the current export performance, the government recently asked exporters to make no more new sales for June and to delay as much as possible shipments at the end of June until July. However, industry sources said, that nobody will listen to this advice.

The May sales brought total earnings from coffee exports this year to $1.13 bln, 253 per cent higher than the $446.89 million earned in the same period in 1996. Revenue last month was $268.96 million against $109.08 million in May last year and $248.07 million in April 1997.

UNITED STATES - The United States Department of Agriculture said it will release its first 1997/98 world coffee production estimate in the World Agricultural Production Report on June 13 after 1900 GMT.

On June 27, USDA is slated to release coffee production, supply and distribution balances - based on the production estimates released earlier - in its bulletin Tropical Products: World Markets and Trade. The bulletin, which also publishes data on US coffee trade and consumption, will be released after 1900 GMT.

JAPAN - Japan imported 463,709 bags of coffee in February 1997, nearly 13 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 930,500 bags, 21 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996.

Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 5.5 per cent to 5.619 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/February 1997 were Brazil (211,700 vs 134,200 bags) and Colombia (190,300 vs 196,700 bags).
